title: ক্ষুধিত পাষাণ (Rabindranath Tagore), Maison edition 54f37caa-050b-47c3-95c2-3cbc214d6485, revision 3cb6a0b9-f774-4822-92e7-d4fc99de2ef4
period_and_place: India, 1890s. Frame story: an 1890s second-class railway compartment and a lamplit railway junction waiting room at night. Told story: Hyderabad state under the Nizam; Barich, a remote cotton-tax post; a lone 250-year-old white marble palace built by Shah Mahmud II on a towering stone ghat of 150 steps on the Shusta river, at the foot of the forested Aravalli hills, no village near; Deccan-sultanate architecture: pointed carved arches, three rows of great pillars in the upper hall, jali screens, a rose-water bathhouse with fountains and marble seats, Persian carpets, deep-blue curtains, crystal chandeliers; the cotton market and a small tax office far off
palette_and_light: moonlit marble white, deep indigo, saffron, rose, old gold; one light family: cool dusk and moonlight on white marble with small warm lamp glints
lens_and_look: painterly illustrated cinema, soft film grain, 35 mm lens, shallow depth of field

characters.narrator: the narrator, a 22-year-old Bengali man, slim, clean-shaven, short side-parted black hair, white dhoti, cream cotton panjabi and a brown shawl over one shoulder
characters.relative: his theosophist relative, a 30-year-old Bengali man with a thin moustache and round steel-rimmed spectacles, white dhoti and black alpaca chapkan coat, a small notebook in hand
characters.storyteller: the storyteller babu, a 45-year-old Bengali man with a square jaw, a thick upturned moustache going grey and a thin scar through the right eyebrow, close-cropped greying hair, long dark-green sherwani buttoned to the throat, white churidar, a dark embroidered round cap
characters.collector: the young cotton-tax collector, a 26-year-old sturdy Bengali man with a square jaw, a thick black upturned moustache and a thin scar through the right eyebrow, short black hair, white sola topi, short khaki English jacket, tight white trousers, riding boots
characters.collector_night: the young collector, a 26-year-old sturdy Bengali man with a square jaw, a thick black upturned moustache and a thin scar through the right eyebrow, red velvet fez, loose white pyjama, flower-embroidered kaba and a long pale silk choga robe
characters.collector_rest: the young collector, a 26-year-old sturdy Bengali man with a square jaw, a thick black upturned moustache and a thin scar through the right eyebrow, short black hair, bareheaded, plain white kurta and pyjama
characters.girl: the phantom Persian girl, a young woman of about 20 with very large dark eyes and a pale face, fully and modestly clothed in saffron silk pyjama trousers, a long-sleeved gold-embroidered bodice under a sheer rose veil-jacket, a small red cap with a fringe of gold coins around her brow and cheeks, curled gold-thread slippers, half-translucent like a memory
characters.meher: Meher Ali, a gaunt wild-eyed old man of about 70 with a long matted white beard and long white hair, barefoot, ragged faded saffron kurta, a tattered grey blanket over his shoulders, a long bamboo staff
characters.karim: Karim Khan, an old Muslim clerk of about 65 with a neatly trimmed white beard, steel spectacles, a white skullcap and a long white achkan
characters.messenger: the unseen messenger imagined as a veiled Arab woman, a faint shadowy figure in a loose-sleeved dark robe, a fine veil falling from her cap over her face, a curved dagger at her waist, rings on her fingers
characters.guard: a huge, fearsome palace guard of the old Deccan court, an African man with dignified features in a kinkhab brocade robe and turban

shared_facial_signature.signature: a square jaw, a thick upturned moustache and a thin scar through the right eyebrow
shared_facial_signature.why: the babu on the train tells the story in the first person: the young cotton-tax collector at Barich is himself twenty years earlier. One signature keeps him recognisable across the frame story and the told story without saying so.
shared_facial_signature.seed_family: all four looks draw seeds from one family (2100 series)

collector_attire: by day the collector wears the sola topi and short khaki English jacket; at night in the palace the red fez, kaba and silk choga (¶ 'তখন আমি মাথায় এক লাল মখ্‌মলের ফেজ্‌ তুলিয়া ...'); in bed a plain white kurta and pyjama. After the whirlwind takes his hat and coat (scene f01s025) he never wears English dress again (f01s026: 'খাটো কোর্ত্তা এবং সাহেবী হ্যাট্‌পরা একেবারে ছাড়িয়া দিয়াছি'), so from f01s026 on he appears only in the night or rest looks
respectful_depiction: no nudity and no gore anywhere. The bathing women of the palace (f01s004, f01s008-f01s010) are never shown: only architecture, water, light, footprints, bangles and scattered silk garments. The phantom girl is always fully and modestly clothed, often half-translucent or seen in a mirror or by her feet alone. The weeping woman of the storm night (f01s032) is not shown: only the dark chamber, rain, wind and a torn, soaked veil. Her imagined history (f01s027) shows a dagger and a poison cup, never a wound
